response.sql:
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT
    sf.zoneref,
    s.entrystat,
    sf.traitcount
  FROM scanfeatures sf
  INNER JOIN sites s ON sf.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
  WHERE sf.traitcount > 489
),
grouped AS (
  SELECT
    zoneref,
    entrystat,
    AVG(traitcount) as avg_traitcount,
    COUNT(*) as record_count
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY zoneref, entrystat
),
total_count AS (
  SELECT SUM(record_count) as total FROM grouped
)
SELECT
  g.zoneref,
  g.entrystat,
  g.avg_traitcount,
  g.record_count,
  CAST(g.record_count AS FLOAT) / t.total as fraction
FROM grouped g
CROSS JOIN total_count t
WHERE t.total IS NOT NULL AND t.total > 0
ORDER BY fraction DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The phrase 'ignoring missing values' refers to standard SQL AVG() behavior, which automatically excludes NULL traitcount values from the calculation. Since the WHERE filter traitcount > 489 would exclude NULLs anyway, this interpretation is natural.

'Total record count across all groups' means the sum of COUNT(*) across all zoneref/entrystat groups after the traitcount > 489 filter. The 'no rows if there is no total' clause is interpreted as returning an empty result set if total is NULL or ≤ 0 (i.e., no matching records exist).
